subject: Discrepant embed-unit attribution / mid-cycle committed capacity & VAT split
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebula-ai.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: acctg@nebula-ai.com
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Unexpected embed-unit charges on Sep invoice (commit mid-cycle)

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you're well — quick one from our side. We received our September invoice and are seeing ~42k embed units billed as "on-demand" on top of our committed pool for the period 2027-09-01 to 2027-09-30. Our contract (attached) shows a committed allocation that should have covered the traffic.

Two things we'd like clarified:
- Why did ~42k units fall outside the commitment (we didn't change client-side configuration mid-month)?
- The invoice shows VAT applied to those incremental units; per our EU reverse-charge guidance in the SOW, we expected reverse-charge (no VAT) on overages for Nebula (EU entity).

I've attached the invoice and the contract for reference and included our accounting mailbox. Could you point us to the usage export that maps tokens/embed-units to the on-demand vs committed buckets? If there's anything you need from our side (account id, sample request ids), say the word and we'll send it.

Thanks — Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Integrations
Nebula AI
liam.oconnor@nebula-ai.com
attachments: Nebula_Invoice_20270901.pdf, contract_NBLA-2027-09-01.pdf

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebula-ai.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, acctg@nebula-ai.com
Date: 2027-09-14T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected embed-unit charges on Sep invoice (commit mid-cycle)

Thanks for the heads-up, Liam — and sorry for the surprise. We're looking into it. To speed triage, can you confirm:
1) The Redwood account id you used (6-digit) and the workspace name.
2) Whether any clients switched models or toggled experimental routing between Sep 1–10 (fallbacks to hosted variants can increase unit counts).

I'm looping in Ben from Billing Ops (cc'd) to pull the usage export and check attribution against your commitment. We'll produce a CSV mapping request_ids -> model_variant -> bucket (committed|on-demand) and a short timeline.

If you can confirm the account id here, we'll start the export immediately. Expect initial findings in 24 hours.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
attachments: usage_export_request_template.csv (empty stub)

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebula-ai.com>, acctg@nebula-ai.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-15T08:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected embed-unit charges on Sep invoice (commit mid-cycle)

Kim / Liam — I pulled a preliminary sample of Nebula's token/embed attribution for 2027-09-01 -> 2027-09-10. High-level notes:
- We see ~41,963 embed units marked as on-demand.
- ~37k of those correlate with elevated fallback rates: the routing logs show ~18% of requests for the workspace initially targeted the committed model (gpt-embed-q3) but redirected to a hosted-compatible variant (gpt-embed-lite) during short regional capacity shortages on 2027-09-03 02:14–02:52 UTC. The lite variant uses a coarser chunking heuristic and reports higher embed-unit usage per request.
- The remaining ~5k appear to be late-arriving replays from a client-side batch that replayed to our ingest endpoint at Sep 7 23:xx UTC and were marked as on-demand due to session timestamp mismatch.

I've uploaded a filtered usage_export (request_id, timestamp, model_variant, units, bucket) for 2027-09-01..2027-09-10 here: https://internal.redwood/usage_exports/nebul a/nbla_20270901-10.csv (link for ops).

Suggested next steps:
1) If Nebula confirms the replay batch is legitimate, we can consider a one-time credit for the ~5k replay units.
2) For the ~37k due to fallback, per our SLA and committed pool rules, we treat fallbacks to compatible hosted variants as on-demand unless a fallback protection rule was configured. If Nebula wants coverage, we can:
   - a) Issue a goodwill partial credit for the capacity-constrained window while we investigate kernel selection behavior.
   - b) Propose a short-term Dedicated burst reservation or a fallback-protection policy to prevent future spillover.

I'll attach the CSV export and a short ops note. Kim — can you confirm if we should propose option (a) or escalate to Credits Review for a formal adjustment?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: nbla_20270901-10_usage_sample.csv (ops export)

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebula-ai.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, acctg@nebula-ai.com
Date: 2027-09-15T13:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected embed-unit charges on Sep invoice (commit mid-cycle)

Thanks Ben — that matches what we suspected. A few clarifications from our side:
- The replay on Sep 7 was an accidental backfill from an internal reprocessor; that's on us and we'd accept a partial credit request for those 5k units.
- On the fallback events: we did not configure a fallback-protection policy; the integration defaulted to the hosted-compatible variant when the committed model's pool showed temporarily unavailable.

We'd like to request:
1) Credit for the 5k replay units (goodwill or straightforward credit is fine).
2) For the ~37k fallback units, we'd appreciate Redwood's proposal for a partial credit (goodwill) while we evaluate switching to a dedicated burst guard. Our Finance team is sensitive to VAT treatment: if a credit is issued, can Redwood confirm VAT reversal on the credited amount and re-issue a corrected invoice? Our HubSpot deal id is NBLA-2027-09-01 (same as the contract).

Attached is the HubSpot link and our PO reference: PO-NEBULA-901.

Cheers,
Liam

--
Nebula AI Accounting
acctg@nebula-ai.com
attachments: PO-NEBULA-901.pdf

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nebula-ai.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, acctg@nebula-ai.com
Date: 2027-09-16T17:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected embed-unit charges on Sep invoice (commit mid-cycle)

Liam — thanks for the quick confirmation and the PO. Next steps from Redwood:

1) Replay credit: Billing Ops will approve a straight credit for the ~5,000 replay units. Ben, please allocate as a post-bill credit and flag for reversal of VAT on that line item.

2) Fallback window (~37k units): because no fallback-protection was active, our standard treatment is to bill on-demand. That said, given the short duration and the regional capacity factor, I'm escalating to Credits Review asking for a 50% goodwill credit on the fallback delta while we:
   - a) confirm the kernel selection trace with Runtime (ETA 48 hrs)
   - b) help Nebula implement a fallback-protection policy or a short Dedicated burst reservation to prevent recurrence.

3) VAT treatment: If Credits Review approves an adjustment, Finance will reissue a corrected invoice with VAT reversal on the credited amount (we'll need your EU VAT id for the reversal entry).

4) Timeline: initial Credits Review decision by 2027-09-18 EOD; corrected invoice (if approved) within 3 business days after decision.

Can you provide your EU VAT id and confirm the PO number to include on the credit memo? Once we have that, Ben will prepare the provisional credit memo and I will follow up with Operations for the runtime trace.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll work to make this right and help plug the fallback gap.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
attachments: provisional_credit_form.xlsx (ops stub)
